note: Explicit server-side permission catalogue. A permission is never inferred from a role label, a client-supplied field or a screen; the server resolves it from persisted grants. Administrative configuration access has no business approval permission.

permissions.description: Edit the current contact profile of an authorized applicant or represented party.
Answer a request for information on an authorized case.
Submit a new application draft for authorization.
Submit a correction that creates a new application revision.
Withdraw an application while preserving its history.
Run deterministic intake and permit checks against the current versions.
Record an authorized reviewer decision on an application.
Issue a simulated permit from a current approved decision.
Propose a source-to-canonical link from declared evidence.
Approve, reject or correct a source-to-canonical link.
Read field-level provenance and trusted views.
Request a correction of a source fact or identity link.
Stage a raw source snapshot without publishing trusted facts.
Write a version to an authoritative source record.
Resolve a quarantined record and assign its responsible queue.
Move a change case to the next permitted state.
Create a versioned fee assessment from approved inputs.
Import a simulated ERP payment event.
Confirm an allocation of settled funds to an assessment.
Link an ERP finance account to a canonical party.
Draft a rule or fee schedule version.
Approve a rule or fee schedule version authored by somebody else.
Publish an approved rule or fee schedule version.
Generate a permit type icon with Muse Image and save a chosen icon for a permit type. Generating an icon never approves, prices or issues a permit.
Register a source dataset with its required bindings.
Create, reassign or end an effective-dated assignment.
Maintain a stewardship queue and its bindings.
Draft an authority policy version.
Publish an authority policy version after an impact preview.
Read stored document versions and evidence.
Read the append-only application audit trail.
Read the configuration catalogue.
Manage fictional demo actors and their grants.
Revoke a server-held session.
Read the service health and schema state.
Open the planning overview: the cases needing attention, the property context, the proposed changes and the source information.
Wake an agent or put it back to sleep. The City Administrator and the Agent Operator hold this grant.
Wake the steward assistant or put it back to sleep, and no other agent. The Data Steward holds this grant; the Agent Operator holds the general wake grant.
Run the intake agent on one case or on the waiting cases.
Run the adjudication agent on one case or on the cases that are in review.
Ask the steward assistant to prepare a recommendation for a task of the Data Steward's queue. The Data Steward and the Agent Operator hold this grant; the assistant decides nothing.
Change the permit-type configuration and the reason codes of the City.
View the property master: the property record, the town map and the parcel card.
Propose a different parcel for an application: choose another locator candidate or find a parcel by number. A steward still approves the link.
Confirm, as the reviewer, that the approved parcel is the right property before a decision.
Return a case to the applicant with an active reason code of the return type. A return is terminal.
Advance a case to the review area of its permit type once no current blocking finding stands in the way.
Ask the applicant for revisions with an active reason code of the revision type and a message the applicant reads.
Open the City view: permit activity, business categories and exceptions across the city, with synthetic data labelled.

Create, edit, soft-delete and read what-if policy scenarios and their revisions. A scenario is held in memory against copies of the published configuration and never changes a rule, a fee, a permit type or an application.
Run a what-if scenario over a population and keep the immutable run snapshot. A run re-scores frozen case inputs and writes no application, finding, decision or fee row.
Read an immutable what-if run: the counts, the cases that changed, the safety signals and the hypothetical assessed fees.
Read and download the deterministic legislator briefing built from a what-if run.
Open the operations dashboard: active cases, ages, intake agent results, decisions and what needs a person, each with its definition. Read only.
Open the audit log: a read-only, paged view of the append-only audit records, filtered by actor type, action and search. It reads the one audit trail.
Look up an application by reference on the support screen: its status, timeline and the comments written for the applicant. Internal notes are never shown.

Answer a help request an applicant sent through Ask the City. The reply and the answered status are recorded together; on a case that can still change it also adds a comment the applicant reads. It gives no power to decide, issue, return or waive.
Record assistance given outside the application as a support case: an optional reference, the channel and a short summary.
Run the fixed list of read-only invariant checks and record that the run happened. A run changes no permit, decision, fee or comment.

Ask Muse Spark to write or explain the briefing of a what-if run from its typed facts, and read those recorded Muse runs. The answer is validated claim by claim; a rejected answer falls back to the deterministic briefing. It writes no application, finding, decision or fee row.
Save a what-if run as draft rule and fee schedule versions through the existing draft commands. The drafts stay drafts: the author cannot approve or publish them, and nothing published changes.

Ask Muse Spark to propose a what-if in plain language, and read those recorded Muse runs. A proposal is validated change by change and is never saved or run until the City Administrator saves it explicitly.
Archive a case with an active reason code of the archive type. Archiving is a soft delete.
Restore an archived case to the status it held. A restore never revives a stale approval or recommendation.
Change the priority of a case between normal and high.
Route a case to a staff member eligible for its stage. Assignment is routing metadata and grants no authority.
Write a comment on a case, either visible to the applicant or internal.

Waive a current intake finding of a waivable type with an active reason code of the waiver type. A waiver never clears a deterministic rule failure or an identity, credential, finance or parcel-clearance check.

Run the intake agent on a bounded selection of cases that wait for it. The selection names an application and the version it was read at; an empty selection, a stale version or an ineligible case refuses the whole batch.
Ask the applicant help assistant a question and record the turn. The answer is drawn from the City's published rules and from the applicant's own case; the assistant never decides anything.
Ask a person at the City to answer a question. The request is the only route by which a member of the City reads the applicant's question.

Receive an answer the applicant help assistant wrote from the City's published sources. The answer is validated against the source bundle it was given, and an answer that fails the validation is never shown.
Reserved. Read the agent operations screens: the agents home, the agent runs and the agent cases.
Reserved. Open the intake queue without processing the selected cases.
Reserved. Decide which agents may stay awake and what each agent may do.
Reserved. Change the permissions a role grants.
Reserved. Run the linking agent on the source records that wait for a master record.
Reserved. Preview what the steward automation would link, before anything changes.
Reserved. Turn the steward automation on.
Reserved. Pause the steward automation.
Reserved. Queue source records for the steward automation.
Reserved. Review a link the steward automation made.
Reserved. Undo a link the steward automation made.
Reserved. Create a new master record from a source record that matches none.
